paper_id: Yang et al. - 2010 - Revisting Tag Collision Problem in RFID Systems
title: Revisting Tag Collision Problem in RFID Systems
motivation: CRC-based collision detection requires >100 instructions and O(l) complexity, becoming the bottleneck for low-cost RFID tags with extremely limited computation capacity.
problem_framing: Collision detection problem formalized as: determining whether f(∨r_i) = ∨f(r_i) using only simple functions feasible on capacity-limited RFID tags.
key_insight: Using bitwise complement f(r)=r̄ as collision function achieves O(1) complexity with only 1 instruction vs CRC's O(l) complexity and >100 instructions.
method_signature: Quick Collision Detection (QCD) using bitwise complement plus 16-bit collision preamble, replaces CRC for faster identification.
evaluation_criteria: Efficiency Improvement (EI) defined as (t_crc - t_qcd)/t_crc, measured alongside accuracy, utilization rate, and identification delay.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: QCD correctness assumes at least two collided tags emit different random integers; this assumption can fail with probability 0.5^(lm) ≤ 0.5^(2l).
evidence_for_taste: more than 63% slots are under utilized
thinking_moves: 识别出计算复杂度是实际系统瓶颈，而非理论最优
将碰撞检测函数设计从复杂CRC重定义为简单布尔运算
先建立CRC-CD的理论效率上界(Lemma 1&2)，再证明新方法的超越性
在严格数学证明(Theorem 1)后仍强调工程可实现性
提出碰撞前导码机制以缩短空闲/碰撞时隙的通信时间
